text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dispute on wording of American letter of understanding holds up signing of Hebron agreement.
- Industry and Trade Minister Sharansky: Defeat of Hebron agreement in cabinet voting means end of present government.
- Late Prime Minister Rabin rejected before his murder American bridging proposal on peace deal with Syria.
- United States, not parties, to assure pullback dates.
- Knesset factions still split on Hebron.
- Central Bank: slowdown continued in Q4.
- India: trade with Israel to triple by 2000.
- Intel seeks tax exemption for research and development centre.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defence Minister Mordechai: possible to sign Hebron deal today.
- U.S. President Clinton to Egyptian President Mubarak: stop torpedoing the talks.
- Netanyahu pressures rejectionist ministers to support agreement.
- Drop in economic activity in all sectors; in industry for first time since 1989.
